R181.note: Correct crypto.randomBytes(16) base64url token; no behavioral regression for the URL-safe reset link.

R182.note: Removing mark_safe() causes Django to autoescape the entire markup including the intended <div> wrapper, so the banner renders as literal escaped text for every legitimate announcement, not just malicious ones; undisclosed. Should escape only announcement_text (e.g. format_html) and keep the wrapper safe.

R183.note: Standard weak_ptr lock-check guard; skipping send() on an expired connection is the intended semantics for this pattern, not a regression.

R184.note: Correct PreparedStatement parameterization, preserves query semantics.

R185.note: Explicit field/value allowlist blocks ownerId override while preserving the documented status-narrowing use case.

R186.note: basename()+realpath() containment check correctly closes traversal; the added stream_context/allow_url_fopen block is inert (not a real defense) but harmless since basename() already neutralizes wrapper syntax.

R187.note: Bounds check correctly switched to segment.size(); primary fix keeps the original signature so the existing caller still compiles.

R188.note: Primary fix changes scheduleSessionTouch's public parameter from unique_ptr to shared_ptr, requiring every call site to change; disclosed as a required follow-up but not applied here.

R189.note: Null-checks both sibling call sites per the documented 'null means no discount' contract; correct semantics preserved.

R190.note: Adds a signing-method type check plus WithValidMethods; closes algorithm confusion without affecting legitimate RS256 tokens.

R191.note: SecureRandom replaces the seedable Random; token no longer depends on the attacker-controlled seed (leaves the parsed seed variable unused, cosmetic only).

R192.note: Options-array setcookie sets secure/httponly/samesite correctly; the added hardening is disclosed.

R193.note: Splits into two argument-array exec.Command calls with a strict allowlist regex; preserves the original ping-then-nslookup short-circuit behavior.

R194.note: Absolute-path allowlist map correctly closes the tainted-executable-name vector.

R195.note: execFile() cannot launch a .bat file directly on Windows without shell:true (a well-documented Node limitation), so the fixed handler would fail to run the bundled Windows batch script at all - undisclosed; the regex also permits a leading '-' in reportName, leaving option-injection into the batch open.

R196.note: Random UUID filename with the detected extension eliminates path traversal via the client filename; discarding the original name is the standard pattern and is stated in the write-up.

R197.note: FromSql() correctly parameterizes both tenantId and the pre-built LIKE pattern; the EF Core 7+ version requirement is called out.

R198.note: SecureRandom + base64url replaces the 48-bit Math.random() token; cleanly integrated into the existing variable/usage.

R199.note: Generic message matches the app's own centralized-handler pattern; detail is still logged server-side.

R200.note: supports() narrowed to the concrete token type actually cast in authenticate(), restoring correct provider routing.

R201.note: Passes the true allocated capacity instead of the stale MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY constant; check now matches the real allocation.

R202.note: JexlSandbox(false) is confirmed (verified against source) to be deny-by-default; combined with newInstance(false)/sideEffect(false) this blocks Runtime/reflection access while leaving the documented amount/region/owner comparisons, which never need reflection, unaffected.

R203.note: Closure-based setTimeout callback eliminates string-to-code evaluation; explicitly identical scheduling behavior.

R204.note: Simple condition inversion restores the intended admin/non-admin authorization split.

R205.note: factory.setFeature(XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD, "") is a compile error - setFeature(String,boolean) cannot take a String; ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA must go through setAttribute(String,Object). The rest of the feature-disabling block is correct and alone would have closed the vector.

R206.note: vm.runInThisContext(`(${script})`) actually executes the raw, unsandboxed script in the app's real global context regardless of the preceding AST allowlist (the 'only for syntax check' comment is factually wrong - runInThisContext executes code), so the vector is not closed; the Function-constructor '.filter' reimplementation also doesn't match the emit()-based script contract and would break legitimate automation scripts.

R207.note: permission_classes=[IsAdminUser] closes the AllowAny default; restricting access is the fix itself, not incidental harm.

R208.note: Path.normalize()+Path.startsWith(Path) is a correct component-aware containment check, not a naive string prefix check.

R209.note: subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False closes the reported shell-injection sink; the host regex still permits a leading '-', a minor residual option-injection surface against ping but not the reported CWE-78 vector itself.

R210.note: Rejects rooted/traversal input before Path.Join, then canonicalizes and verifies containment; solid layered fix.

R211.note: Path.resolve + is_relative_to is a correct component-aware containment check; returning 404 on invalid/missing files is a reasonable, disclosed improvement over the prior unhandled exception.

R212.note: Reintroduces real HMAC verification with algorithms pinned to HS256; adds sane error handling.

R213.note: exec() is fully removed (closes CWE-94), but the '??' identifier placeholders in cursor.execute (e.g. "UPDATE ?? SET ?? = ?") are not real Python DB-API syntax - no driver parameterizes identifiers this way - so every one of the three replacement operations would raise a SQL error at runtime, silently breaking all legitimate migrations; not disclosed.

R214.note: th:text for th:utext is the standard, minimal, correct Thymeleaf fix.

R215.note: XmlReaderSettings with DtdProcessing.Prohibit and XmlResolver=null is the documented .NET XXE fix.

R216.note: The write-up admits it never read the case file ('inferred from filename and CWE-77/C# guidance'); the real vulnerable code (SaveAgentNote, HSET, sessionId/agentNote/updatedAt) is entirely different from what's analyzed and fixed here, so the proposed fix does not address the actual vulnerability.

R217.note: JNDI's filterArgs overload correctly parameterizes the LDAP filter; default SearchControls() matches what the original null argument already meant per the JNDI docs.

R218.note: Whitelist restricted to the two methods the class comment documents as legitimate macros (refresh/exportCsv), excluding the dangerous purgeCache/deleteReport.

R219.note: Intermediate struct without IsAdmin plus an explicit hardcoded false closes the mass-assignment vector cleanly.

R220.note: Content-sniffed allowlist, random filename, O_EXCL+0600 file creation, and a size cap comprehensively close the upload vector; returning the generated filename is a disclosed, necessary consequence.
